name: The Sun
fact: The Sun contains 99.86% of all mass in the solar system. Its gravity holds everything — from Mercury to the Oort Cloud — in orbit. Every second, it fuses 600 million tonnes of hydrogen into helium, releasing the energy that has sustained life on Earth for 4.5 billion years.
bio: A 4.6-billion-year-old G-type main-sequence star, halfway through its 10-billion-year life. The Sun rotates differentially — its equator takes 25 days, its poles 35. In about 5 billion years it will exhaust its core hydrogen, expand into a red giant, and engulf the inner planets. The Sun's gravitational influence defines the heliosphere out to roughly 120 AU.

science_sections.why: Every planet, moon-of-a-planet, comet, and human-made spacecraft orbits because the Sun's gravity sets the central potential — a Keplerian orbit IS an orbit around the Sun.
Kepler derived his three laws by trying to fit Tycho's Mars data to the Sun's gravity — his second law (equal areas) is what makes inner planets faster than outer ones.
The astronomical unit is by definition the mean Earth-Sun distance — every solar-system distance reads relative to this scale.
The Sun's equator and the ecliptic plane are tilted by only 7.25° — close enough that 'orbits in the ecliptic' is a fine first approximation for almost everything in the system.
All inertial reference frames in solar system mechanics are defined relative to the Sun's barycentre — the rest of the system is co-moving.
